title: Signs of ΔH and ΔS: physisorption, diamond to graphite, protein denaturation and propene to cyclopropane
summary: Four processes, measured one after another on a virtual bench. N2 molecules stick to charcoal while an adsorption calorimeter reads the heat and the Sackur-Tetrode entropies of a 3-D gas and a 2-D film give ΔS; a diamond lattice opens into graphite sheets while a Hess ladder built from two combustion enthalpies gives ΔH; a protein unfolds in a DSC cell while the endothermic peak is integrated for ΔH and ΔS = ΔH/Tm; propene closes into cyclopropane while a second Hess ladder and third-law entropies give its signs. Sign meters swing for each value, every process lands on a ΔH-ΔS sign plane, List-II is matched and options A-D are tested entry by entry. No prediction stage - input, run, watch, result.
subject: Chemistry
topic: Signs of enthalpy and entropy change - adsorption, allotropes, protein denaturation and ring strain
subtopics: Enthalpy change and heat flow at constant pressure
concepts: Physisorption: a van der Waals attraction forms, so heat is released (ΔH < 0); a 3-D gas becomes a 2-D film, so ΔS < 0 - entry (2)
Diamond to graphite: ΔH = ΔcH(diamond) - ΔcH(graphite) = -1.9 kJ/mol; S(graphite) > S(diamond), ΔS = +3.36 J/K mol - entry (5)
Protein denaturation: hydrogen bonds break (ΔH > 0); the unfolded chain has many more conformations (ΔS > 0) - entry (1)
Propene to cyclopropane: ring strain makes ΔH = +33.3 kJ/mol; closing the ring freezes the CH3 rotor, ΔS = -29.5 J/K mol - entry (4)
Only option C (P2, Q5, R1, S4) matches all four; (3) ΔS = 0 fits none of the processes

methods: Solved independently before any key was consulted: P2, Q5, R1, S4 - option C
Hess's law two ways for Q and S (combustion and formation enthalpies agree); third-law entropies for ΔS

Physisorption ΔS from Sackur-Tetrode 3-D and 2-D translational entropies; the formula checked against S°(N2) = 191.6 J/K mol (translation + rotation); ΔS < 0 across 50-298 K and 0.16-0.3 nm² per molecule
Two-state DSC model: the peak area integrates back to ΔH within 0.5%; ΔS = ΔH/Tm > 0
Controls: chemisorption still (2); reversing Q, R or S leaves no printed option
Independent script tests/verify_p1q13.py: 31 of 31 checks pass
Solution websites: MathonGo's published solution (their Q45) gives C
The page computes every ΔH and ΔS at run time from the data and models, then reads off the signs, the List-II entries and the option; no answer is written into the script

Headless-browser suite tests/sim_p1q13.js drives the whole page: the engine and its controls, the answer above the experiment and the dock below it, conditions and warnings, the automatic eight-stage run, the gauges reading ΔH before ΔS, tiles, board, badges, charts, the reveal, the ΔG-T explorer, replay, pause, reset, a custom run, classroom mode, 390 and 360 px, reduced motion, the feed entries and the real app shell opening it
Answer cross-checked afterwards against the official final key printed with the Paper 1 PDF: Q13 -> C
verification.note: Representative values are used where the question names a class of process: N2 on activated charcoal (≈ -15 kJ/mol) for physisorption and a lysozyme-like two-state protein (ΔH ≈ 500 kJ/mol, Tm ≈ 347 K) for denaturation; the signs, which are all the question asks, do not depend on the choice.
